summary: Tool invocation orchestration overhead causing streaming timeouts and elevated p95 latency
description: Issue summary: Several customers reported elevated end-to-end latency and streaming connection timeouts when using models that invoke external tool calls. Impact: Customer streaming sessions hit client-side timeouts (120s) and saw p95 generation latency increase by ~300-600ms per tool invocation. The customer (Parcelly) uses a dedicated route with tool-call enabled for address-normalization and observed degraded user experience in their checkout flow.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the Redwood streaming chat endpoint with a prompt that triggers a tool call to the address_normalizer tool (route: /v1/chat/stream).
2) Enable function/tool calling via the SDK and set max_stream_timeout=120s client-side.
3) Observe response times and streaming disconnects in the client after ~90-110s or abrupt streaming stop when tool invocation occurs.
4) Reproduce with curl using request-id header for trace: curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'x-request-id: rq_87af3d' -d '{...tool call...}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream

comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported multiple streaming disconnects when invoking address_normalizer. Provided request-ids and sample payloads. Noted that the issue began 2026-03-09 after a runtime rollout.

Alejandro Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial metric sweep indicates spike in p95 token latency on routes that hit tool-invocation path. Dashboard: /dashboards/latency/tool-invoke shows +450ms median extra. Flagged orchestration change on 2026-03-08 (deploy id: orch-2026-03-08-a) that enabled synchronous schema validation for tool responses.

Parcelly Support Rep (customer) 2026-03-10: Confirmed they saw increased latency in checkout address validation flow. They can reproduce consistently with their production dataset and want a mitigation ASAP.

Ravi Patel (SRE/Assignee) 2026-03-11: Temporarily backfilled a canary rollback for orch-2026-03-08-a on the customer's dedicated pool. Observed immediate reduction in p95 for the route. Working on a safer permanent fix.

Eng (Orchestration) 2026-03-12: Found that the new validation path performs sync call to schema-validator for every invocation and cache was accidentally disabled due to a key-salt change in PR 4123. Also, network retries to tool-proxy were set to 2 with 100ms backoff; combined this increased tail latency.

Ravi Patel 2026-03-12: Implemented workaround: re-enable cached schema results and set schema-validation to async-with-timeout=100ms with permissive fallback. Deployed to canary; Parcelly confirmed improvement. Planning full rollout after QA.

Maya Chen 2026-03-13: Customer accepted workaround as mitigation. Coordinated on release window and confirmed no further streaming disconnects after workaround applied. Closing as resolved but tracking follow-ups.
Note: Link to incident Slack thread: #incidents-tool-invoke-22401
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: New orchestration change made schema validation synchronous, adding 200-600ms per tool call.
Hypothesis 2: Cache miss rate increased because of new cache-salt introduced in PR 4123; validation could not reuse prior results.
Hypothesis 3: Additional network retries and auth handshake added extra round-trips before tool execution.

Findings: Correlated deploy orch-2026-03-08-a with latency jump. Log traces show schema-validator end-to-end ~320ms on average, handshake/auth ~120-200ms. Cache miss exploded from 8% -> 72% on tool interface lookups.
Quantified impact: For a single tool-invocation, added median +420ms and p95 +780ms. Multi-invocation prompts multiplied impact leading to client streaming timeouts.
Temporary mitigation validated: Re-enabling cache and switching to async validation reduced p95 overhead to +60ms. Canary rollback matched pre-deploy baseline.
Testing notes: Added unit and integration tests for cache-key stability and a perf regression test to gate schema-validator changes.
resolution_notes: 1) Applied canary rollback of orch-2026-03-08-a on affected dedicated pools (parcelly's pool) 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC which restored baseline latency.
2) Implemented a permanent fix in orchestration: schema-validation runs async with a 100ms timeout and permissive fallback if validation does not complete in time (PR 4129).
3) Restored and stabilized schema-validator caching with consistent cache-salt semantics (PR 4130).
4) Reduced tool-proxy retry policy to 1 with exponential backoff starting at 50ms to avoid compounding latencies (PR 4131).
5) Deployed changes to canary 2026-03-12 and full rollout to production 2026-03-13 after QA validation. Monitoring shows p95 returns near pre-change baseline and customer reported fix.
6) Customer follow-up: Parcelly asked for a post-deploy verification window; SRE provided a 72-hour verification report and added the route to enhanced latency alerts.
Rollout notes: Added a feature flag (tool_call.async_validation=true) for safety and a perf regression test to the CI pipeline to block future synchronous validation changes without perf review.
postmortem_followup: Owners: Orchestration (Ravi Patel), ToolProxy (Dalia Nguyen).
